MIGRATION 0134 APPLIED + APP HALF (219b175) - invoices.payment_method gains 'balance' for prepaid credit settlements. THE REQUEST THAT PRODUCED IT SAID "no migration needed, payment_method is free text". It is NOT free text and there were TWO gates: 0025's CHECK constraint and 0039's pay_invoice() body, which raises 'Invalid payment method: balance'. The RPC gate fires FIRST, so shipping the app half alone would not have written a wrong label - it would have made EVERY prepaid settlement fail outright, a live outage on the money path. 'balance' is a bookkeeping LABEL, not a debit: the money was already consumed at delivery by lib/prepaid.ts's FIFO walk and the pay action only records and locks - no amount, balance, VAT figure or ledger row moves. NO BACKFILL, deliberately: prepaid+cash rows (the mislabel this fixes) and payment_mode=null rows (pre-0037, unclassifiable) stay exactly as recorded, so any report splitting cash from balance must expect the pre-0134 period to read cash-heavy. THE PREPAID GUARD IS THE POINT, not the widened allowlist: pay_invoice() resolves mode snapshot-first then falls back to the customer's project, which is EXACTLY what the UI does (payment_mode ?? projectPaymentMode) - any other resolution puts a refusal behind an enabled button, and a NULL snapshot is not evidence of 'not prepaid', it is evidence no snapshot was taken. THE FILE ON DISK WAS RECONCILED TO WHAT RAN: the applied guard wraps the project lookup in count(distinct ...) = 1 so a future mixed-mode customer resolves to unknown and FAILS CLOSED; the draft used a plain scalar subquery. 0099/0100/0101 precedent - correction recorded, not squashed. CREATE OR REPLACE (not drop+recreate) because the signature is byte-identical to 0039's, satisfying the 0038 one-signature rule by construction. Verification block D is a STANDING audit, not an apply-time reading: zero rows forever where payment_method='balance' resolves non-prepaid, and its mode resolution is a deliberate byte-copy of the guard's - an audit that resolves differently from the rule it audits reports its own disagreement as a finding. Change both in one commit.

MIGRATION 0137 APPLIED + APP HALF (9603778 SQL, 0b46a6a app) - OUTSTANDING REFLECTS THE LIVE PREPAID BALANCE. A confirmed invoice's amount_due_sar is frozen at confirm, so for a PREPAID customer a top-up arriving after confirmation covers work the invoice still shows as due - the receivable was overstated. Rule: prepaid outstanding = least(frozen, greatest(0, shortfall - already_taken)); postpaid comes out byte-unchanged. THE CAP CAN ONLY EVER REDUCE A RECEIVABLE, NEVER INVENT ONE. It is a VIEW because the balance is a plain sum (topups - sum of consumedAmount) - the FIFO walk only decides the covered/unpaid SPLIT, not the total - so SQL can express it without reimplementing lib/prepaid.ts. Three views: v_customer_prepaid_balance (SQL mirror of derivedBalanceItems, VAT rounded PER ITEM), v_invoice_outstanding_live (newest-first allocation window so two invoices cannot claim the same riyal), v_receivables_open (first nine columns byte-identical, two appended - 42P16 is append-only). ABSENT MEANS ZERO IS A PROPERTY OF THE VIEW: it emits a row for every confirmed unpaid non-void invoice INCLUDING the 0.00 ones, so each consumer's ?? 0 is a fact not a fallback - and the if (!is_paid) branch is GONE, not kept alongside. app/trips/InvoicesModal.tsx is DELIBERATELY LEFT FROZEN - that is the document's own number on a per-document row and must keep matching the printed invoice. 0137 failed its first apply on 42P16's TYPE face (least()/greatest() returns bare numeric where the column was numeric(12,2)); section 6 was corrected because of it.

MIGRATION 0138 APPLIED (d5c9271) + THE APP FIX (6109f3b) - THE STRANDED SPECIAL CHARGE IS CLOSED. This was the one open DECISION carried in this file for weeks; Turki made it, and the framing that decided it was: all app data is DUMMY - we are not fixing fake balances for their own sake, we are fixing the STRUCTURAL LOGIC so it is correct when real data arrives. MIGRATION 0139 APPLIED + THE WHOLE APP HALF (2c9103e, 8 files) - YOU CANNOT ARCHIVE AWAY A DEBT. Three parts that are one feature: THE BLOCK (archiving refused while money is owed TO US), THE RETURN (a prepaid customer in CREDIT is archivable and the leftover is money WE owe THEM), THE WRITE-OFF (a manager may force the archive with a REASON - not a bypass, a decision: the debt is written off, zeroed and attributed). NOTHING HERE INVENTS A NUMBER. THE SIGN CONVENTION IS THE LOAD-BEARING IDEA: amount_payable_sar < 0 means owed TO US and BLOCKS; = 0 settled; > 0 is credit we owe THEM, allowed with a return offered. Turki stated it as two rules (prepaid, postpaid) because he states owed as a positive quantity - they are THE SAME RULE once the sign is fixed, and collapsing them to one expression is the point. RECORDING IS NOT DEDUCTING: customer_balance_returns is NOT a top-up, nothing in the balance chain reads it, the balance figure is deliberately unchanged - which is exactly why the 'Returned' mark has to travel beside the figure everywhere (BalanceWithMark is the ONE component that renders figure-plus-mark). THE AMOUNT IS NOT A FIELD AND MUST NEVER BECOME ONE, on either side - return_customer_balance() reads it from v_customer_amount_payable and freezes its own copy; the modal SHOWS it read-only. Q5 IS THE ONE LOOSE END: 0019's archive_project() is still in place and is an UNGUARDED BACK DOOR - every app call site is on archive_project_guarded, so the DROP is unblocked and bare, architect's call on timing.
